title: Hive
description: Describes the structure of a hive: its nodes, the edges between them, any strobe emitter registrations, and any surfaces or strobe surface registrations. Loaded once to build the initial hive structure. A hive can contain multiple directed cyclic graphs created from the nodes and edges.

name.description: Canonical name of the hive. Named by a teleport node's destination to reach a node in this hive from another one, so it must be unique within a collection of hives loaded together.

nodes.description: Nodes contained in this hive. Each node's name must be unique within this nodes array; edges and strobeEmitters refer to nodes by this name.

strobeEmitters.description: Registers a subset of this hive's nodes as periodic strobe emitters. Only a node of type SceneRootNode can be registered. A strobe emitter is what drives scripted nodes: it sends a strobe action into the graph at a fixed rate, running the coreScript of each scripted node it reaches. Registering a surface in strobeSurfaces publishes what those scripts produce; an animated scene needs both.

surfaces.description: Surfaces exposed by this hive, e.g. for display or input. Each surface's name must be unique within this surfaces array; strobeSurfaces refers to surfaces by this name.

strobeSurfaces.description: Registers a subset of this hive's surfaces to be strobed periodically, causing each to update/regenerate at a fixed rate. This collects and publishes what the hive currently holds; it runs no script of its own, so on its own it publishes only geometry set directly in JSON. See strobeEmitters for the other half.

nodeName.description: Name that uniquely identifies a node within this hive's nodes array.

actionFlag.description: Used to describe the type of a particular graph action. Some actions carry more than one, and an edge naming any one of them admits that action. PING_GRAPH_ACTION: a ping action. SERIALISABLE_GRAPH_ACTION: an action that can be teleported to another hive, carried by ping and trigger actions, and the only flag a teleport node acts on. SCRIPT_GRAPH_ACTION: an action that runs a node's coreScript, carried by script actions and by the strobe action that drives them. SCENE_GRAPH_ACTION: the action a surface runs to collect geometry and transforms into itself. SCENE_STROBE_GRAPH_ACTION: the action a registered strobe emitter sends out at a fixed rate. ANIMATE_GRAPH_ACTION: the action that carries an animating mode out from the node that set it. AGENT_GRAPH_ACTION: the action an agent node emits to carry one conversation from node to node. TRIGGER_GRAPH_ACTION: the action emitted by a trigger node, by a script's trigger() call, or by a model's emitTrigger tool. AGENT_AFFECT_GRAPH_ACTION: the action a node sends out across its edges when an agentic request starts or stops directly affecting it, so that other nodes can react to it too. Sent only by a node whose emitAgentAffectAction is set; on scene geometry it arrives as that node's agent-visible flag being set.

nodeType.description: Identifies a kind of node, so that something visiting a node can recognise what it has arrived at. GRAPH_NODE is reported by any node that does not identify a more specific kind of its own.

capability.description: How capable a model must be to service a request. LOW: can do simple tasks well. MEDIUM: can do average tasks well. HIGH: can do complex tasks well.

vertexVisibility.description: Controls when a vertex is displayed. ALWAYS: always visible. AGENT: visible while an agentic action is being applied. GRABBED: visible when in a grabbed state (e.g. a mouse button held down). DRAGGING: visible when being dragged (e.g. a mouse down then move). HOVERED_OVER: visible when hovered over (e.g. a non-button-down mouse over movement). Consecutive vertexes sharing the same visibility are grouped together.

edge.description: A directed link from a node to another node within the same hive.

toNodeName.description: Name of the node, within this hive, that this edge is directed to.

actionFlags.description: Restricts which types of action may cross this edge: an action can only traverse it if its own action type matches one of the flags listed here. If omitted or empty, this edge places no restriction and any action may traverse it, with one exception: an agent action requires a named match and never crosses an unrestricted edge, so a route meant to carry one must list AGENT_GRAPH_ACTION. Listing flags also gives an edge precedence when a node picks which single edge an action crosses: where an action could cross either, an edge naming an action type it matches is taken ahead of an unrestricted edge, whatever order the two appear in. An unrestricted edge is therefore a fallback route rather than one competing on position. Whatever the flags say, an action never crosses the same edge twice on one pass through the graph, so a cycle is walked round once rather than endlessly.

actionsCompleteAfterTraverse.description: Whether an action completes once it has traversed this edge. The node the edge leads to is still applied to as normal, but that application is the action's last: it never goes on to cross a further edge from there, however many remain permitted. If omitted or false, the action carries on as normal once applied to that node.

strobeEmitter.description: Registers a node as a periodic strobe emitter, causing it to emit a strobe action at a fixed rate.

nodeName.description: Name of the node to register as a strobe emitter. It must be a node of type SceneRootNode.

periodMs.description: Emission period in milliseconds (time between successive emissions).

surfaceName.description: Name that uniquely identifies a surface within this hive's surfaces array.

strobeSurface.description: Registers a surface to be strobed periodically, causing it to update/regenerate at a fixed rate.

surfaceName.description: Name of the surface to register as strobed.

periodMs.description: Strobe period in milliseconds (time between successive strobes).

nodeLocation.description: Identifies a node by the hive that contains it and, if that hive is hosted remotely, the host machine it can be reached on.

hostname.description: Hostname of the host machine, if left blank, a hive within the current hive collection is assumed.

port.description: Port that the host machine listens on.

hiveName.description: Name of the hive that contains the node.

nodeName.description: Name of the node in that hive that contains it.

vertexFields.description: The geometry a vertex carries, shared by both ways of writing vertexes. Not a form that can be used on its own.

posn.description: Position in right hand cartesian coordinates: In order X, Y, Z. By default, one unit maps to one millimeter.

colour.description: Colour: In order Red, Green, Blue, Alpha.

texCoords.description: Texture coordinates: In order U, V.

normal.description: Normal in right hand cartesian coordinates (must be normalised): In order X, Y, Z.

groupedVertex.description: A single vertex of a piece of scene geometry, within a vertex group that states the visibility for all of them.

vertex.description: A single vertex of a piece of scene geometry, carrying the visibility of the group it belongs to.

visibility.description: When this vertex is displayed. Visibility belongs to a group of vertexes rather than to a vertex: each run of consecutive vertexes sharing one visibility forms a single group, and a run that returns to a visibility used earlier opens a new group rather than rejoining the earlier one. Each run should therefore be a whole number of triangles, since a triangle split across two groups is left incomplete in both. Omit for ALWAYS. Writing it out per vertex like this suits geometry that is mostly one visibility; use vertexGroups instead to state it once for a whole group.

vertexGroup.description: A group of vertexes that share one visibility, stated once for the whole group rather than repeated against every vertex.

visibility.description: When the vertexes of this group are displayed. Omit for ALWAYS.

vertexes.description: Vertexes making up this group. Each triplet defines a triangle with counter-clockwise winding order for the front face, so a group should hold a whole number of triangles.

transform.description: 4x4 transform matrix, standard column-major order of elements. Translation components are in scene geometry units; by default, one unit maps to one millimeter.

nodeBase.description: Fields common to every node, regardless of concrete type.

type.description: The type of the hive graph node.

pokeEnabled.description: Whether poking is enabled for this node.

edges.description: Edges directed from this node to other nodes in this hive. A node carries at most 32 of them.

scriptSource.description: The pair of Lua scripts that a scripted node runs. coreScript runs when an action that runs scripts reaches the node, which in a running hive means once per strobe, so it is run repeatedly. It may optionally define two entry points as globals: init(), which is called once and once only per node, on the first run that reaches it, for work that must happen exactly once, and invoke(), which is called on every run. The body of the script outside those functions is run in full on every run until either entry point exists, so a script that defines one has its top level run only once and is entered through those functions thereafter, while a script that defines neither is simply run top to bottom every time. A script defining only init() therefore builds itself once and then does nothing on any later run. pokeScript runs only when the node is poked, and only if pokeEnabled is set, and has no such entry points. A coreScript may also define getToolCallBindings(capability) as a global, declaring tool calls this node offers a visiting model on top of the fixed set its node type already carries. That one is not an entry point: no run ever calls it, and defining it does not close the top level down the way init() or invoke() does. It is called only while an agentic request is being applied to this node. See LuaNodeAPI.md.

coreScript.description: Main Lua source code that this node runs when invoked, optionally by way of the init() and invoke() entry points described above.

pokeScript.description: Lua source code that this node runs when poked.

scriptNodeBase.description: Fields common to every node that runs Lua. Not a node type in its own right; mixed into the concrete scripted types, currently SceneGeometryScriptNode, SceneTransformScriptNode and TriggerNode.

pingNode.description: A simple node that just provides a ping point.

teleportNode.description: A node that teleports any serialisable action it receives to another node, possibly hosted by a different hive. Ping and trigger actions are the serialisable ones. A trigger carrying a name or type restriction that this node does not itself match is passed over and never forwarded, so a trigger meant to leave the hive must be unrestricted or must name this node.

destination.description: Location of the node that receives actions teleported through this node.

sceneRootNode.description: A node that roots a visual scene, and the only node type that can be registered as a strobe emitter. It is a source of actions rather than a target of them: nothing is applied to it as an action passes through.

sceneGeometryFields.description: Scene-geometry payload shared by SceneGeometryNode and SceneGeometryScriptNode. Mixed into both; not a node type in its own right. Vertexes are written either as a flat vertexes array carrying a visibility per vertex, or as a vertexGroups array stating one visibility per group. The two describe the same thing, so a node carries one or the other and never both.

vertexes.description: Vertexes making up the scene object this node defines, as one flat list. Each triplet defines a triangle with counter-clockwise winding order for the front face. Geometry that is all one visibility, or nearly so, is shortest written this way; anything carrying sizeable runs of a visibility is better written as vertexGroups, which states it once per group instead of against every vertex.

vertexGroups.description: Vertexes making up the scene object this node defines, gathered into groups that each state their visibility once. Groups are built in the order given, and their vertexes reach a surface in that order. This is the same structure the scene itself holds, so it is the form to reach for when a node carries geometry of more than one visibility.

emitAgentAffectAction.description: Whether marking this node's agent-visible flag also sends that change onward across its edges, so downstream geometry can react to it too. If false, the flag only affects this node. Only applies to the flag being set automatically while an agentic request is applied to this node; a script-driven change to the flag never sends it onward regardless of this setting.

sceneGeometryNode.description: A node that represents scene geometry, with vertexes set directly rather than by a Lua script.

sceneGeometryScriptNode.description: A scripted node that represents scene geometry, with vertexes that can be populated by a Lua script. Holds an animating mode, and offers a visiting model the tools to read and set it. Vertexes are appended and never cleared, so a script that builds fixed geometry must build it exactly once, either from init() or behind a guard on the vertex count.

sceneTransformFields.description: Fields shared by SceneTransformNode and SceneTransformScriptNode. Not a node type in its own right.

emitAgentAffectAction.description: Whether an agentic action directly affecting this node also sends that onward across its edges, so downstream nodes can react to it too. If false, the effect stays local to this node.

sceneTransformNode.description: A node that represents a transform applied to scene geometry, set directly rather than by a Lua script.

sceneTransformScriptNode.description: A scripted node that represents a transform applied to scene geometry, which a Lua script can read and modify via getTransform()/setTransform(). Holds an animating mode, and offers a visiting model the tools to read and set it.

agentPrompt.description: A single prompt, paired with the node it is sent for. As an agent action traverses the graph, each node it reaches is matched against these entries in order and the first entry that matches supplies the prompt sent for that node. A node matching no entry is passed over silently.

nodeIdentifier.description: Name of the node this prompt applies to. Omit or leave empty to match on node type alone. This names a node anywhere the action reaches, which need not be a node of this hive.

nodeType.description: Kind of node this prompt applies to. Must match for the prompt to be used, whether or not nodeIdentifier is set.

prompt.description: Prompt sent when this entry matches the node being visited. The model answering it is given the tools of that node on top of whatever the harness assigned to the NODE role, so a prompt can ask for those tools by name. See modelTools.md for which node type offers what.

terminateOnResponse.description: Whether the action completes once this prompt's response has been processed, rather than continuing on to match further nodes it reaches.

agentNode.description: A node that holds a set of prompts and emits them as an agent action, driving one conversation onwards from node to node as that action traverses the graph. The conversation is carried forward across every node the action matches, so later prompts see what earlier ones produced.

capability.description: How capable the model servicing this node's prompts must be. Every prompt this node sends is requested for the NODE role at this capability, so a harness must carry a model assignment naming exactly that pair for this node to run at all.

prompts.description: Prompts the emitted action sends, each paired with the node it is sent for. Matched in the order given.

autoTriggerAgentAction.description: Whether a trigger arriving at this node emits an agent action. If false, this node holds its prompts but never emits them in response to a trigger, leaving emission to something else.

serialiseEmittedActions.description: Whether actions emitted by this node are queued so that only one is ever in flight at a time, the next starting once the current one completes. If false, a node triggered again while an emitted action is still running starts a second conversation alongside the first.

triggerNode.description: A Lua-scripted node that exists to emit trigger actions on behalf of an AI model. An agent action reaching this node offers the model a tool that emits a trigger action from here, optionally restricted to a node name and/or a node type, so the model chooses what part of the graph fires next. The emitted action is never applied back to this node, so it cannot trigger itself. It takes no part in a scene, so it holds no animating mode and a strobe never reaches its coreScript: that script runs only under an action that runs scripts. The Lua bindings it has are the ones every scripted node carries and no more: NodeType, trigger(), and the ToolType constants a coreScript declares its own tool calls through.

emitTriggerOnPoke.description: Whether poking this node emits a trigger action of its own, unrestricted by name or type, once its pokeScript has run. The pokeScript runs on every poke either way; set this false to leave emission entirely to that script or to the model.

node.description: Concrete nodes that can be added directly to a hive.

surfaceBase.description: Fields common to every surface, regardless of concrete type.

type.description: The type of the hive surface.

default.description: Whether this surface is the default surface of its kind within this hive, i.e. the one handed out when a surface of that kind is asked for by no particular name.

graphHiveSceneSurface.description: A surface that enables the contents of a visual scene pathway to be viewed and interacted with.

sceneRootNodeName.description: Name of the SceneRootNode, within this hive, that this surface is bound to.

initialFocusNodeName.description: Name of the node, within this hive, that the scene camera should initially centre and zoom on. Omit to have the camera fit the whole scene instead. Applied once, when the camera is first set up.

focusViewportFraction.description: Fraction of the viewport height the focused node's bounds should span when the camera is first set up. Ignored if initialFocusNodeName is not set.

surface.description: Concrete surfaces that can be added directly to a hive.
